utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, kindly call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Jadranko Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Today is Tuesday, good afternoon to the Defence counsel, the accused, the OTP representatives, and all the people assisting us in our task. I believe that Mr. Kovacic wanted to say something. Is it so? Do you want to take the floor or not, Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR.  KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. No, I don't have any procedural questions before we start. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's have the witness brought in. Madam Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Just one procedural matter. I was under the impression initially that the Prosecution was given two hours for cross-examination and then I understand that there is a possibility that it is actually only an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, an hour and a half. You understood well.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I, nonetheless, am going to make a request for at least an extra half an hour, and I do that bearing in mind the direct testimony of the witness and the questions that came from the Bench. I think that Your Honours have expanded the subject matter here and it will require appropriately at least another half an hour from the Prosecution for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I shall ask my colleagues. Yes, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to respond. As far as time is concerned, we all know that the time that the Chamber took for its own questions belongs to a separate category of questions by the Judges. I can't imagine a situation in which the OTP would need more time for their cross-examination because of something that occurred during the questions being asked by the Judges. The OTP got 50 per cent more time than the Defence, and I don't think the Chamber should grant this request for additional time. It was on very few and rare occasions that the Defence asked for additional time to examine a witness and actually got it. Second, regardless of how much time the OTP may or may not be granted, obviously there is a tendency here to expand on the subject matter, which means that I'll probably have some questions in re-direct which will yet again take up more time later on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I would like to clarify with Mr. Kovacic, he said, and I quote, that: "The OTP got 50 per cent," 5-0 per cent, "more time than the Defence and I do not think the Chamber should grant this request for additional time." Now, I believe that the OTP has not been given 50 per cent more time, but it was given the same, I mean 90 minutes, which the Defence originally used. And that is why I think that the 50 per cent is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, I agree -- [Interpretation] I agree with your math, Your Honour. What I meant was, given the fact that the Defence got one hour and the Prosecutor got one and a half hours, that's 50 per cent more than the time we were granted for our examination-in-chief. But I think basically we are talking about the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: If it please Your Honour, I would respectfully support my learned friend's response and I do object to the application orally put forward by my learned friend for the Prosecution. I believe it was the witness, the one before last, that was subject to a similar application by the Prosecution. On that occasion, on behalf of Bruno Stojic, we did not intervene or make any representation. However, as a matter of procedural law, it's my submission that when Your Honours determine and allocate time to the parties, the party moving for additional time should show, in my submission, that matters have arisen in the course of examination-in-chief that could not have been reasonably anticipated. In other words, matters that were not in the reasonable contemplation of the cross-examining party. Your Honours, rather than being a cause for additional time, it's my respectful submission that given the length and depth of Your Honours' questioning indeed many areas were covered and clarified in relation to this witness's testimony that takes a burden and a significant burden at that, away from the Prosecution's shoulders. So, Your Honours, in my submission there's been no good cause put forward by my learned friend as to why an additional half an hour is needed. The area of the witness is very discrete, very clear, and in my submission an hour and a half is more than sufficient to get to the nub of this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Petkovic Defence supports the position adopted by our learned friends on this side of the court. Your Honours will know that throughout this case in many respects the Defence have never been that enthusiastic about the time-limited approach to examination of witnesses, but that is the approach consistently adopted throughout the case. It's the approach that's been applied to us and it's the approach which should be applied throughout. And looking at it now, what happened according to -- in accordance with Your Honours' guide-lines, is that the Prosecution were given an hour and a half. The way Your Honours do it, an hour was to match the hour that Mr. Kovacic had for his witness and the other half-hour was to match the half-hour that the other Defences were given. Now the Prosecution were then, therefore, entitled to that hour and a half Your Honours gave them that to start with whether or not we actually used that 30 minutes, but we didn't, and that is the real position. So the real position is that there has only been an hour of examination from the Defence side. There has, of course, been fairly extensive questioning by the Judges, but what my learned friends say I adopt there, which is that Your Honours have, in fact, clarified a number of issues, you've made it unnecessary to deal with a number of issues. And if the Prosecution now want extra time, they must as Mr. Khan clearly pointed out, they must demonstrate exactly why it is they need it and what has expanded the area of cross-examination. Because, really, this report is in a very clear, discrete area. Your Honours' questions were directed to matters in the report and they just don't need any more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Judges are going to confer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam West, could you explain to us why you need additional time? What is your reason? Since Mr. Kovacic had one hour, we had granted 30 minutes to the other Defence teams, that is one hour and a half, and generously enough, we granted you an hour and a half as well, whereas normally, based on the case law of other Trial Chambers, it's 50 per cent for cross-examination, I say that from memory. So you have had one hour and a half which is 50 per cent more than Mr. Kovacic. Why do you then need additional time?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think perhaps I should have said this initially, but I think the disadvantage that the Prosecution has with an expert witness, particularly one that is offered to the Chamber based on a report, is that the counsel, the expert's counsel, can put his entire opinion in through a written submission and then highlight the parts that he thinks are important. However, the disadvantage that I face is that I have to go through the entire report and cross the entire report. I cannot take out just the highlights that were focused on by counsel. So I think it's inherent in the act of putting on an expert witness who is submitting a report that it makes it quite difficult for the cross-examination to be limited only to an hour and a half. And that's why I would submit that two hours is not an unreasonable request and it is only a half an hour more. I also will note for the Court that I understand that there have been several expert witnesses put on by the Prosecution, for example, I would just note that there was a sniping expert that the Prosecution witness -- excuse me, the OTP put on for the Chamber used two hours, yet the defendants or the accused counsel were granted four hours for cross-examination. Your Honour, that's the basis of the Prosecution's request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to discuss the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may, just a single detail bearing in mind this new element that my learned friend has just brought up. I do have to say that the sniping expert, the example that they brought up, was the only case in which the Defence got additional time because the material was very comprehensive, and the remaining three cases, with all due respect, as far as I remember we got maybe a little more time than the Prosecutor for their chief. At any rate, the Prosecutor has already got 50 per cent more time; that is the reason. And that is the discrepancy that we are talking about and that we have so far tried to comply with. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may just say a single sentence. It was with great interest that I followed the arguments put forward by my colleague Ms. West, and I remember that the Defence used the same arguments during the OTP case when we talked, when we cross-examined more or less all of the expert witnesses of the OTP. It is in that context that I would like to remind you all that the military expert, Mr. Pringle was in this courtroom and that the Defence of Mr. Petkovic, General Petkovic, despite the written submissions that we had filed beforehand and all the arguments that we put forward got a single hour for cross-examining this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I just make a two-sentence observation on what Ms. West said just now. The point that she made in her last comments is a point which, if it applied at all, applied at the beginning. It hasn't changed. That would have been an argument for asking, whether good or bad, it would have been an argument for her to put forward asking for more time right at the outset. Your Honours gave an hour and a half at the outset. That point is not a change at all, so it doesn't justify any additional time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After deliberating, the Trial Chamber has decided to grant another 30 minutes to the Prosecution, but I shall express separate opinion on this issue and the Trial Chamber reserves the right to decide to grant additional time to the Defence if need be, to the Praljak Defence if need be. My own opinion is as follows. The Trial Chamber is granting 30 minutes, but I personally fail to see the purpose or the usefulness of it because I see the question as being very clear. Was a charge positioned on the very structure of the bridge or not? That's the very question at the heart of the matter. This debate was started by the Defence and by the Judges' questions, but it may be that I did not understand anything. So therefore, you have got another 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I think it should be that the majority opinion is also reasoned, and you will allow me to say that in the majority's view, the equality of arms mainly gives the right to each party to have the time it needs for an effective presentation of its case. Here it is true that the Judges have asked an enormous amount of questions yesterday, and it is also relatively time-consuming always to have these DVDs again and again. And we have always said that we were flexible so that's why we agree here to extend the time, but at the same time we also are prepared to accept for time for re-direct on the side of the Defence, and this would be a gift time not counted towards your general credit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before the witness appears I do have another matter to raise. I was about to give it up, but after I read the OTP's letter that I got a minute before you, Your Honours, appeared in this courtroom, it is only now that I begin to see the meaning. Just before you came to this courtroom today, Your Honours, we got a letter from the OTP informing us that they would disclose to us a DVD not meant to be part of their cross-examination, one that has not been disclosed as part of the Rule 68 material. It is not exculpatory. Still, they were about to disclose this document to us because some issues were raised yesterday. The letter seems to suggest that the Prosecutor is serving on us a DVD containing the results of forensic tests, various kinds of footage, recordings of the destruction and eventual collapse of the Old Bridge in Mostar in November 1993. And then they go on to say: "The analysis was conducted by," and now the original [In English] " ... the digital technology and biometric department of the Netherlands Forensic Institute Ministry of Justice and was received by the Office of the Prosecution on June 24." So that was last week, if I'm not wrong. [Interpretation] In the meantime, Your Honours, my colleague has tried to skim through this DVD just to see if it's worth anything at all, given the fact that the Prosecutor said they wouldn't be using it. Given the three minutes and given the technology available in this courtroom, the only thing we could conclude at this moment was that we simply have to go through this, we have to study this before we resume with this witness. It's quite likely that this very material contains things that we might be using on re-direct. It may even call for further tests and analyses, and this is something that as we all know the OTP failed to do during the presentation of their case, although they actually had a theory as to why the bridge was destroyed. If I look at the title of this analysis, and bearing in mind the two minutes that we've actually managed to see, we simply have no choice but to seek to have at least another half-hour to study this material and see what it's all about. This is something that might have a significant bearing on the procedural status of both parties, not just the Defence but also the OTP. Secondly, this is something that I've never seen so far. I've never seen this happen at this Tribunal, but I move that the Chamber at least address a formal admonition, a caution, to the OTP, if not actually some formal kind of punishment because this might be relevant material, it might even be exculpatory but we don't know that yet. Yet, this is disclosed to us two or three minutes before the Chamber walks into this courtroom midway through the evidence being given by this witness, the very witness that this material is related to. And although the Prosecutor claims that this is no Rule 68 material, and although the Prosecutor claims that they only got it a week ago, on the 24th of June, I think this makes no difference. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, I'm absolutely flabbergasted. How is it that this DVD material which seems to be connected to expert work on the destruction of the Old Bridge was disclosed only a few minutes before the witness, the expert witness, came in as part of the cross-examination? What happened?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours, and to everyone in and around the courtroom. Douglas Stringer appearing on behalf of the Prosecution. This is a disclosure matter so I'm going to take this. I don't -- I think that the situation is not quite as dire or severe as it's been indicated by counsel or perhaps the extent to which Mr. President's indicated in his comments. I can tell you very briefly what this is about. The Prosecution received the report of Professor Jankovic on the 9th of May, that's the Defence expert report submitted by the Praljak team. We received it on the 9th of May. When we -- and actually, we had to wait approximately a week or so after the date the report was filed to obtain the videos themselves that Professor Jankovic relied on in his testimony and in his report. The videos accompanying the report did not actually come to us until about a week or so after the report of the 9th of May. When we finally got the videos, and these are the videos referred to by Professor Jankovic, the two clips, the ORF2 and the Mostar TV videos, we looked at those and we noticed that on one of them there appeared to be a discontinuity. Now, Professor Jankovic said a good many things yesterday that are not referred to or contained in his report. One thing that's not contained in his report is reference to any discontinuity in either of the video-clips that he reviewed and made a part of his findings. Now we know from his testimony yesterday that he did observe in one of the clips, the ORF2 clip, that there is a discontinuity. He referred to it, and it's actually -- everyone can notice that when they look at the video, but it's not referred to in his report and we didn't know what he would say about that. So we determined that we should see if we could get someone to look at Professor Jankovic's videotapes to give us an opinion as to whether there is, in fact, a discontinuity which is found in one or both of those. And so at that point, and now we're into mid-May or the third week of May, we decided to try to send those out to have an expert look at them and that's what we did. And together with the two video-clips that are referred to by Professor Jankovic in his report, we added a third video-clip -- actually, we sent a number of video-clips to the Dutch forensic lab and asked them to look at all of these. Let me say this first of all and as clearly as possible. Everything that was sent to the Dutch forensic lab and which is referred to in the report that came back to us last week is in the possession of the Defence, has been in the possession of the Defence or was disclosed to the Defence years ago, years ago. We're talking about the two clips that are part of Professor Jankovic's report; we're talking about Exhibit P 1040, which is the other clip that Ms. West used in her cross-examination yesterday; and we're talking about a couple of other clips of basically the same footage that are in the possession of the Prosecution, were disclosed to the Defence years ago, but which haven't been used during the trial. So I want to be clear, Mr. President, there is nothing -- there is no new material, there is no new video material that we're talking about here. After we received the Jankovic report, we sent these materials out to the Dutch to see if they could determine whether there was any discontinuity or whether we were just interpreting the video incorrectly. We did this in order to prepare ourselves for the cross-examination of Professor Jankovic. We just received the report and the disk that came back from the Dutch last week. My letter's actually incorrect. The report is dated the 24th of June, we received it on the 25th is what I'm told. We looked at it. It doesn't contain anything new. There aren't any disclosure requirements that are raised by the video in our view. Only after yesterday's proceedings when Mr. Kovacic stood up and indicated a desire or a wish that, if possible, one could play the recordings side by side, that it might be useful to him, that we went back last night, we talked about it further this morning, and in fact that's what essentially this video DVD is that came back from the Dutch forensic lab. It simply takes all the videos and runs them in a synchronised fashion, all the videos which they've always had. We discussed it last night, we discussed it further this morning, and we decided out of an interest in full disclosure or to assist Mr. Kovacic in his review of these materials, for whatever reason, we would disclose it. We had to make the copies for all the Defence, we wrote the letter, we regret that it wasn't disclosed earlier, but that's just the nature of the beast, if you will. Mr. President, there's nothing new and in our view it doesn't raise any significant issues in respect of this witness or this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Mr. Stringer, what is the conclusion drawn by the Dutch lab?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, we -- if I could just take a step back. We decided that for purposes of cross-examination there's no witness to come tell you about that and maybe we could do that at a later time, but what they've done is to note that among the various footages of the destruction there is discontinuity and we know that. And what the report essentially does is to tell us where the discontinuities exist among the different clips that you see. I mean, it would be the Prosecution's submission that in fact this report shows that the ORF video footage, and I think the witness was admitting this yesterday when he talked about the discontinuity, that the footage of the initial water fountain or water wall in terms of its being juxtaposed directly ahead of the collapse of the bridge, there may be a question whether, in fact, there is a lapse of time. But of course, we all can see that there is a lapse of time before the bridge collapses and we see that in the other video which was always in evidence here, which is P 1040. So the report essentially confirms what we had sort of thought among ourselves about the timing of the water wall that Mr. Jankovic bases his report on and then the subsequent collapse of the bridge which now indicates or demonstrates, in our view, that the water wall on which he relied actually occurs some minutes before, at the very least -- actually, we don't know how much time elapses between the water wall and the explosion that Mr. Jankovic talks about and then the subsequent collapse of the bridge. We don't know how much time elapsed between those two events because all of the video has breaks in it at certain times. But when you synchronize them all, it's clear that the water wall which forms the basis of Professor Jankovic's opinion is not the event that actually causes or precedes immediately the collapse of the bridge. So that's what we think the report -- those are just my -- just answering your question, that's my -- I guess, my understanding of what the report says. But getting back to the basic point, it's something that we've used. We wanted to learn about discontinuity. We learned yesterday for the first time that there was, in fact, agreement about discontinuity. We didn't know that at the time we received his report because Professor Jankovic doesn't talk about it. So that was the reason why the materials were sent out. It was in response to the report that we received in mid-May and the videos. We received the report. We looked at it. And then again, in light of Mr. Kovacic's remarks yesterday, we decided to disclose it. That's really all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, unfortunately this will take more time than it actually merits, but I would like to make three points here. The first point is I would like to compliment my colleague for the detailed information that has just been given to us, and I would like to thank my colleague for testifying and for providing us with an analysis of the evidence that is still in front of us or the case that is still ongoing. And I would kindly ask you to disregard it because you are supposed to draw conclusions after this evidence has come in. Secondly, the Defence of course cannot talk about the value or quality of the material that was disclosed to us seven minutes ago because we have not been able to go through it. However, the title itself of the material that was disclosed to us and the name of the institution that carried out this analysis, in light of the additional information provided by our colleague as to what the analysis contains tells me that it would be necessary for us to at least look at it, to go through it, to see what this is all about. The alternative for us in the Defence is simply to put our trust in the Prosecution and to take everything the Prosecutor told us at face value; and what he has told us is, for all intents and purposes, that there is nothing there. And, Your Honours, with all due respect for the Prosecution, I have been trained not to trust the Prosecution, just as they have been trained not to trust the Defence. And you are the ones who should put your trust in what one or the other side tells you. So I will not -- I don't want to accept the explanation provided to us just like that. I want to do my own verifying. And the fourth thing is we heard about the time-line, they received the DVD, there's nothing new there. I agree with them, there is nothing new there except for one thing, and that is the opinion -- the opinion of -- of a respectable institution, at least based on its name. And we, I think, should have the right to go through it. And to conclude, if it is true that the Prosecution received this material on the 25th of June, that was last Thursday if I'm not mistaken -- I think it was actually Wednesday. The expert came here on Thursday and we had the first briefing session on Friday, it lasted for about an hour, and it would be reasonable, then, for us to have been able to go through it on our own and then to ask our expert to look at it. So I don't challenge the claim that all the video recordings - and I have to accept what the Prosecution has said - that all the recordings that the institute has seen, that we have already seen them all because the Prosecution disclosed everything to us, we disclosed everything to them. But I would like to know what the opinion was of the institute. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Kovacic, the best solution -- wait, wait. I will give you the floor in a moment. Mr. Kovacic, you asked for 30 minutes to watch the DVD, so the best now is to pause for 30 minutes and enable you to watch the DVD and maybe this will help you after you have seen it. Maybe there will be no new problem. You asked for 30 minutes. The best solution is for you to watch this DVD.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. This will assist us, but I still stand by what I proposed at the beginning, and that is that you at least reprimand the Prosecution, at least in moral terms, for failing to disclose this to us on the 25th or the 26th because it -- that would have saved us the half an hour that we're about to spend and heaven only knows what we'll find there and whether there will be any need for any further discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry, before my learned friend. Your Honour, as far as trust is concerned, I think on behalf of Bruno Stojic, it's not a matter of trust. Of course I'm more than ready to accept undertakings from the other side of the courtroom, from the Prosecution bar, and I would hope that they would be willing to take undertakings and accept undertakings from the Defence bar on relevant matters. I think the issue alluded to by my learned friend Mr. Kovacic is one of professional responsibility, yes, and that can be cured, at least in part, by some time, half an hour, to be granted. What I'm not clear on, and the issue to which I'd like some clarification, am I correct in understanding that the Prosecution is not intending to show this video to the witness and use it in evidence? Is it simply disclosed to the parties rather than a document or an exhibit that they seek to put to the witness today? If it's the second, I would have submissions to make on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Taking Mr. Khan's point first, Mr. President, as we've indicated in the letter, it has never been the intention of the Prosecution to use this report or this video during the cross-examination of Professor Jankovic. That's number one. Secondly, going back to Mr. Kovacic's remarks, Mr. President, there's nothing to remand the Prosecution for and we reject any suggestion that the Prosecution's acted improperly or anything less than fully transparent and appropriately. If counsel led evidence and expert testimony on the basis of videotape that has defects or has discontinuity which sheds light on the opinions, that's his problem, that's not ours. He could have sent these out years ago and got the same opinion that we did when we sent them out only after receiving their expert report. We didn't know what the issues would be until they gave us their report. Counsel could have done that years ago, and it's his own fault if he's surprised about what's contained in the video. That's number one. Number two, we disclosed this simply out of good-will. There is no legal obligation to do so. We are entitled to take their expert reports out and to show them to other expert reports and to perhaps try to get a little more peer review than this witness got. And the information that we learn when we go to experts to try to prepare our cross-examination of their experts is not something that we have to give to them. It's not our job in this system here at the Tribunal to give them our cross-examination outline of their expert witnesses. It's not our responsibility to call Mr. Kovacic and tell him what we're going to do on cross-examination with his expert witnesses. We're entitled to prepare ourselves, and that's what we've done. And only after Mr. Kovacic expressed a desire to have simultaneous or synchronised videotape yesterday did we decide out of a courtesy, a professional spirit of cooperation, to share this with him should he wish to use it. We're not tendering it, we're not tendering any reports or findings of the Dutch. It was simply disclosed and there is no improper conduct on the part of the Prosecution here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, one word, if I may, one word. [Interpretation] We're not claiming that this is new material. There seems to be a misunderstanding here. We believe that this institute of the justice ministry of the Netherlands, that they saw the materials that we have seen here in the courtroom and that we all have, but it is a fact. And this is the only thing that we're talking about, that the Prosecution received this material and it appears to be an analysis, on the 25th of June, as our colleague has indicated, so one day before my witness came here to The Hague for the briefing. I was in The Hague, the Prosecution knows that, and I could have gone through this with the expert and it is up to me to decide whether this is exculpatory or not, whether this is the Defence case or not; but in this case, I am bereft of this possibility. So I thank you for giving us at least this half an hour for us to be able to go through it. It may really be meaningless, I agree, but it may be of critical importance. I just don't know that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we are going to pause for half an hour and we will resume at half past 3.00, and therefore this will give you the time to watch this DVD.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We resume now, and just before the witness comes in there's a question to the Prosecution. The video which you showed us yesterday which seems to feature explosion, smoke, and then the bridge which is -- remains still for a moment, where does that particular video comes? Who shot it?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is Exhibit P 01040. It was tendered into evidence a year -- July 4th of 2007. The witness who tendered it was Denis Saric, and it was -- oh, may I have a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Pardon me, Your Honour, Mr. President, I stand corrected. It was given to us by Denis Saric, however, it was tendered by Delalic, D-e-l-a-l-i-c, on July 4th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So it is Denis Saric who shot this video?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour. May I have a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: It's my understanding, and I will clarify this to ensure that we're giving the correct information to the Court, but I understand that he didn't shoot the video, he didn't take the video, he recorded it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, during the 30 minutes you had the time to see the video, what is your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we have gone through this as much as we have been able to. You received this paper just a moment before you entered the courtroom, so I don't think that you were able to actually go through it. I would just like to make a couple of points and make a proposal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I can work very fast. I don't need 30 minutes to take recognition of the document and I saw the conclusion immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I agree, but in light of the numbers for the videos that we're talking about that are being analysed, in order to be able to really grasp what this is all about we have to first look at the scene that appears under this number to be able to know what we're talking about. But what I wanted to say, first, it is undoubted - and that stems from the chapter entitled "Observations" at page 3 of 10 that this analysis contains - having analysed this chapter we can conclude that a certain video with the number 2389 and another one numbered 2777 is in fact the video that we saw yesterday in the courtroom, that bears the number P 01040. And in the observations it is further noted that the TV ORF1 [as interpreted] that the analysis, that the expert analysis relied on and the one that we saw in P 01040 were taken by the same camera and that the so-called Mostar video that we discussed with the expert yesterday and that is mentioned in his analysis was taken by another camera. So if we go back, the expert in simplified terms told us quite clearly, and this is in the transcript, that the analysis was done on the basis of two video recordings. One is the ORF2 and the other one is the so-called Mostar video. And the expert himself told us that a discontinuity was noted on the ORF2 video, and that is why they controlled it by looking at the other video, Mostar video, and the expert report of this witness indicates that the time-line, the chronology, of events is absolutely the same. In other words, despite the discontinuity that exists in the video recording, the time-line is the same, the sequence of the events is the same. And then the Prosecution showed this other exhibit which shows that the sequence of events after the smoke and the flash and the water wall is different because the bridge does not collapse, it collapses some ten seconds after that. But perhaps I'm going too far here. My proposal is the following. It is obvious that this analysis has not contributed to the Prosecution case substantially and it could not really cast any doubts on the expert witness's report and testimony, at least in my opinion; otherwise, they would have used it in their cross-examination. So it seems to me that this analysis actually confirms one of the basic arguments and that is that two cameras, two tapes, are what the analysis relies on and they're identical. So if anything, this expert report that we have just received supports the reasoning of the expert witness and his claims. But in order to be fair, I maintain what I said at the beginning. The expert should have been in the position to see that. I should have been able to show this to the witness who is a literate man, an expert person. He went through all the materials that we have and they, the two -- the experts, decided to use the two videos that were taken by two different cameras. And I propose that we give this to the expert, to let him go for today, to call him back to the courtroom tomorrow, and then before the cross-examination continues, the Defence should be entitled to ask him whether the expert report that he had been able to read overnight, whether it in any way changes his opinion and that would be our ground zero. We would proceed from that. And then the Prosecution could continue with the cross-examination. The second thing is -- the second option is to deem it irrelevant and to forget about its existence and I'm not in favour of the second option. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will confer with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, excuse me -- excuse me, Mr. President, sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Wait a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. What do you want to say, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just a few brief remarks in response to those of Mr. Kovacic. First of all, Mr. President, just to again state what's obvious, that this is a Defence expert called by a Defence team, and the analysis that is done is one that could and perhaps should have been done by the Defence since they're the ones who are tendering the videos and they're tendering an analysis and an expert opinion on the basis of the videos. That's number one. Of course we do not agree with the conclusions or the suggestions of counsel in respect of the meaning of the report and its impact or its evidentiary value. In fact, the report is not in evidence, and as we've indicated it was never our intention even to offer it into evidence, at least not at this stage, because it was received late. It was received to enable us to prepare for cross-examination and only for that purpose. If we were to tender it, it would have to be at a later stage during the Prosecution rebuttal case. And the fact is that this analysis is one that requires there be a witness in the box who can testify about it, who can tell the Trial Chamber how it was prepared, who can elaborate and answer the Trial Chamber's questions and indeed the questions of the parties in respect of the report, in respect of the video that was done. And I don't think it's going to be useful to anyone to try to have Professor Jankovic comment on it when, number one, it's not in evidence; and secondly, no one here really knows the basic information that the Trial Chamber requires in order to assess the report itself. Thirdly, Mr. President, just the logistics of what Mr. Kovacic is proposing. Because the Prosecution didn't intend to use or to tender this report, it's not been translated and I think that there are logistical language issues in respect of Professor Jankovic's ability to review it and to assimilate the information and then to comment on it in a meaningful way here. It's not in the B/C/S and it's not in French, so I think that's another impediment. So our suggestion simply, Mr. President, is to do what we had always intended which is to leave it aside and come back to it at a later time, maybe we will, maybe we won't. It was simply offered, again, as a good-will gesture or in fairness to Mr. Kovacic based on his remarks from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber has heard the parties and has decided that the witness would come in and the Prosecution will ask him -- will examine him as cross-examination for about an hour, and during the questions the Judges, if they consider that it's useful, questions will be asked from the witness specifying that the witness is not an expert on videos or on footage for stills which have been taken by the videos. But the Defence will be able during re-direct to come back on these matters. So let's have the witness in the courtroom. Madam Usher, would you please go and get the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please be seated. Sorry for the delay. We had to settle a procedural matter. We should have started at 2.15. Basically we're going to start at 4.00, but that's life, c'est la vie, and all our apologies for you having to wait. I'm going to give the floor to Madam Prosecutor, who's going to proceed with her cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Professor. I hope you had a good evening. Professor, since you left here yesterday, have you spoken to anyone, whether in person or by the telephone, regarding your testimony here yesterday?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not speak to anybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you some questions regarding the issue of discontinuity. You mentioned this several times yesterday, and specifically on page 30100 of the transcript you were commenting, this is the transcript which you don't have in front of you but I'll read it, you were commenting about the discontinuity you saw in the TV ORF video. Do you remember talking about that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that well because that's the fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Correct. And let me just cite for you what you said to remind you. This is on 30100, it's line 12, and you said yesterday: "If you look at the ORF2 footage, the impression is that two pieces of footage have been glued or pasted next to one another as if the camera -- as if there was a camera filming up to the moment of collapse and the other one would have filmed the collapse itself. The impression is that the first part was filmed while somebody was handling the camera because you see the moves by the cameraman, and the second footage seems to be a fixed camera." Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, because that's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And I'll just direct the Court to page 30112, it's line 17, you further testified in speaking about again this discontinuity that: "The movements that we can see are those of someone handling the camera." A few moments later you then followed up and said: "If it were not for that footage," and here you're talking about the TV Mostar footage, "I would not be here today because there is no continuity in the TV ORF footage." Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember, but could -- can I express my opinion on this movie or the footage that I saw yesterday for the first time?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We're going to speak about that in one moment and you can express it then. Let me ask you another question going back to discontinuity. You appear to consider it to be a very important part of the TV ORF video; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, everything is important.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: But notwithstanding, you spoke about it extensively yesterday; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, why didn't you mention it in your original report, the report that you submitted to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we submitted in our report is an analysis carried out by the three of us, and it's a technical report. So we did not include in that report impressions, things that had not been proved.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, you submitted that report as an expert report to this Trial Chamber. Shouldn't that report have been your full and thorough analysis of the events?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I -- no, no. I tried yesterday to explain that I saw, I and my colleagues, this discontinuity but that we thought that the two pieces of footage corresponded to one event that we saw on the -- in the other footage, in the other video.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, are you again suggesting that you understand that these two events -- rather, these two videos are the same event?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I have no proof that it is not so; therefore, we thought that it was one and the same event but it could be two. We have no evidence. We cannot say that it is one or two events. It's impossible to say so.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, we've spoken about this issue of same event several times before. Yesterday you noted that in your report you indicated that these two videos reported one event, that it was the same event. On direct testimony yesterday, four separate times you indicated that these two videos were the same event. On cross-examination, you again noted four separate times that these two videos were the same event, and I'll direct your attention to 30128, line 18, where you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down when giving numbers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: -- when you said: "We thought it was the same event and we still believe it." However, on cross-examination late in the day you then testified that you were not certain that the two films shown were one and the same event. Professor, after seeing Exhibit P 01040, you have not seen it fully and we'll go back to it, after seeing that exhibit, what is your answer today? Are the events leading up to the collapse in TV ORF and in the TV Mostar video the same event or are they a different event?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me start with the beginning. We believed - and believing is one thing, facts can be different - we believed that this reported one single event when we wrote our report. We had no reason not to believe so, but we realized that in the first video we had, in fact, two pieces, that's obvious. It is, therefore, normal for me to tell you in the beginning that we thought that this was one single event. When you showed me our video, of course then I realized now, this is my belief now, I think this has to do with two events. And when you ask me what I think now, what I'm thinking, I can explain. In your video, which is more or less the same as the first video that we got; right up to the collapse of the bridge, the two videos are more or less the same. I don't know if they are the same, but they're more or less the same. I did not notice any difference between the two. So everything we said yesterday about the dot of light, the water wall, the black smoke can be seen in both videos. So technically speaking, we say in a similar case, as can be seen in your video, it was a missed destruction. They tried to destroy the bridge, in other words, but they failed to, something failed to work --

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, let me stop you there. Assume for the purposes of my question that you now believe, just assume for the purposes of your answer, that in fact the events leading up to the collapse on those two videos are different events. If you now understand that to be a fact, would you change your opinion about the cause of the collapse?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It would not have changed my opinion, but I would say that the probability might have been lessened a little. Why? Allow me to finish what I was trying to say before. So I'm now talking about your video, the one I saw yesterday. We saw all the elements in a concatenation towards the explosion, but we did not see the destruction, we did not see the light ball or the spot of light. That means that the detonator was activated but the explosion did not take place, that can happen sometimes, I don't know --

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, sorry for the interruption again --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had this on several occasions --

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... you can then speak about it -- excuse me, Professor --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me finish answering your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Professor, please answer the questions as they are asked. Do not add any other comments.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I answer the question strictly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What did you want to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I wanted to say was that we spoke about the destruction of the bridge with a projectile, everything stays the same, nothing has changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Madam Prosecutor, you're going to show us this video again, P 1040, but please give us the sound as well, the soundtrack, because yesterday we were shown footage without the soundtrack and I would like to hear whether there are people speaking, whether there are detonations. Normally it would be possible to hear that.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Indeed, if we can have the sound, we will do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, the reason I stopped you was for that very reason. We're going to play the video and you can explain it along the way. While we're getting that video you just said though your opinion wouldn't have changed, the probability might have lessened a little bit. Yesterday you said you were 80 per cent sure; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. If now the probability has lessened a little bit, what percentage sure are you now?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's say 75 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I proceed? I believe there will be sound.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, I'm going to play the video from yesterday again. I'm just going to start it at the beginning, although we stopped at about 5.26. We're just going to start right ahead from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, we're now at 5.28. We saw your water pillar at about 4.26. We're about a minute later. You will agree with me that the bridge still stands; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's obvious.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I'm going to play up till 5.40, and I will ask you to focus at about 5.38 and then I'll ask you a question.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, right before I stopped it, it was right at 5.38. Did you see a little skip or a jump or some discontinuity in the tape?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. You need much more time to see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to go back again and we'll try it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, did you see that skip in the tape?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we look at things like this in slow motion.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. We'll try this one more time just to ensure that you're clear about what I'm looking for. I'll again direct your attention to 5.38.8.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, did you see the skip in that tape?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I saw a skip, a downward skip, of the footage.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, if you can assume for the purposes of this question that there was a skip --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A downward skip, I'm saying that to the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. If you can assume for the purposes of this question that there was a downward skip or a cut or a splice, would you agree with me that, in fact, there had to have been a stop in filming, there was a period of time that was not filmed?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: All right. Well, yesterday you spoke about the concept of frame by frame, and you told the Trial Chamber that it was very important that you examined the period of time before the collapse frame by frame. So you know what concept means; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And the reason it's important to examine something frame by frame is to ensure that you're not missing anything on the video; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No -- well, on a frame-by-frame analysis we used that in order to see what was -- what caused the bridge to collapse. So I said, if it was because of a projectile, we should have seen the projectile before the bridge would collapse; or else, when we wanted to analyse at what time we saw the spot of light, the water wall, and the black smoke, we needed to analyse frame by frame to see whether the times would tally.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to continue the video and we're going to go to 5.55, and right before 5.55 I would ask that you focus on the events on the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, did you just see the video frame either skip or was cut or what might be called a splice?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to back up just to ask you another question about that and play it again, and I'm going to ask you whether the video, in fact, changes vantage point.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Did it change a vantage point?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before you spoke we saw some images, some frames, so, you know, I couldn't really react. The images went by.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I'll do it again and slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And I just want to ask you about one more difference and it regards the smoke that we now see at 5.55.1. I'm going to back this up and ask if you see that smoke in the frame immediately before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So would you agree with me that again here we have another splice or another cut in the tape?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably so.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Would you also agree that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Witness, I don't want to interfere with Madam Prosecutor in her questions, but like everybody I'm following this footage very carefully and I imagine the following hypothesis and you'll tell me straight away whether this is wrong or it can have some merit. When the Prosecutor started playing the footage we saw that there was this water wall and then black smoke. Thereafter we could see the bridge still standing. Looking at this, I wondered whether there was not a shell that hit the water before the bridge, the shell exploded, and that could cause the smoke. And now just watching a few seconds ago the other frame, my impression is that a shell hit further than the bridge, may have hit a building, for instance, that there was some smoke that rose and it seems to be seen in the picture and because of the wind it went back, the smoke went back towards the bridge. Am I wrong? Am I right? What do you think?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I remember properly, in some videos that we did not use as evidence I saw projectiles, more specifically one, that hit, as you said, a building behind the bridge; if I remember properly, it happened exactly the way you described it, it's possible. But I would not -- the two water streams are different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Prosecutor, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: You just said that the two water streams are different. I'm not sure I understand what you mean. Do you mean the water activity we see on TV ORF is different from the water activity we see on the TV Mostar video?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I said that the linear water gush that we saw in the three videos, the two that we introduced and the one you presented, are totally different from the water activity resulting from the fall of a projectile into the water or a ricochet, a projectile that would hit the water. That cannot be mixed up, it's totally different, of course for those who know the effects -- the facts.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. Going back to this video, we're now at 5.55, and I'm just going to back up again and play it.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Did you just see the skip in the video and the smoke in the sort of -- above the bridge?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I could see the smoke but in a continuum, in the second part.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, does the smoke suggest that there might be another impact somewhere?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is to be found in the second part of the video you showed us or you're showing us.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, my question is: Does this smoke --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the cut. Can I finish? Therefore, the smoke may be as the Presiding Judge said and as I saw in other videos, namely, that there was a projectile that hit something behind the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So, Professor, you would agree with me that this smoke, in fact, indicates some sort of impact?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to continue to play the video for about 20 more seconds --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I've been very patient, I really have. However, if you look at the heading, at the title of this analysis, if you look at the content and if you look at the evidence of this witness so far, it just doesn't follow that we have before us an expert in video analysis. This is simply not true. The subject of this evidence is an analysis of the destruction of the Old Bridge based on such video footage as is available. That is what this witness is here for. He's not an expert in interpreting all sorts of detail that he's now being asked about. Any one of us laymen could perhaps comment on all these features, but this is simply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, let me stop you. The Prosecutor is trying to make a demonstration. Let's follow her. We're now at the stage of smoke, of smoke, and I think the smoke results from a previous hit beyond the bridge. The witness we have in front of us is not contradicting me. Let us wait and see. Now the counter is 5.55.4. Let's see the rest. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Since we are now at 5.55, at this point the water pillar, you remember, was at 4.23, we're already about a minute and a half later. And you will agree that the bridge still has not come down; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in your video, yesterday's video, that was true, as you said. After the water wall, the wall -- the bridge remained intact. So technically we say that it was a missed trial. We -- one tried to destroy the bridge, one activated the detonator, we could see the spot of light, but the main charge was not ignited. That's my interpretation of your video.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. But in my video, the video that you see in front of you, this is the same water pillar at 4.26 that you saw on your video, TV ORF; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to be absolutely certain I should compare in further detail, but my impression was that it was the same. It was my impression.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I'm going to continue to play this video up until about 6.15 and then I will ask you another question.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, at about 6.08 you saw the collapse of the bridge; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: All right. Do you want to see it again?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to give you my opinion on this video I should have to watch it as I can see it in my computer, quietly, in slow motion, but -- because if I fail to see something I watch it frame by frame. It would be too dangerous to give you whatever opinion it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can your assistant from now on play it frame by frame?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I can play it frame by frame.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Right now we're at 6.06 and we're going to go frame by frame through the collapse.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, frame by frame, please. But this is cutting, this is not frame by frame. We simply don't have the sort of technology available to view this frame by frame. We don't have it. This is a series of cuts. If my learned friend is convinced that that's what it is, I'm afraid I have to disappoint her and announce that that is not what it is. As I said yesterday, we are simply unable here in this courtroom to perform this sort of analysis. This is something for a forensic expert in a darkroom and that's how it must be studied. We need at least three pairs of eyes to be able to conduct this sort of analysis. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... you have now 6 minutes, 6 seconds, and 7, so in theory there should be 8/10th, 9/10th, 6 minutes, 7 seconds. Isn't it possible to go either by second or by tenth each frame? Because when we see the bridge collapse, as already we have seen several seconds go by.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour, counsel is correct, that is second by second, not frame by frame. I can continue and we will inquire as to whether it can be done frame by frame in the courtroom. We were able to do it frame by frame, I think, on another video. I'm not sure if we can do it on this one, but I'll inquire. Mr. President, may I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be of assistance, Your Honours, the analysis that we talked about this morning at 4.10, the Dutch analysis -- [In English] "The assumption has been that the different video footages were recorded at the typical speed of 25 frames per second." [Interpretation] This same standard is applied in our own analysis. There are several references in this analysis to these frame-by-frame images, ORF page 3, for example, 0 seconds, 40 milliseconds, 80 milliseconds, and so on and so forth. This is something that is simply not available in this courtroom. My colleague is talking about frames, but we have 25 frames in a second and this is not something that we can reproduce in this courtroom. This is a technical delusion. It's like someone takes me to a dark forest in the middle of the night and tries to convince me that I can actually see anything, which just isn't true. My learned friend should be bringing an expert here who dealt with that sort of thing. Here we have Professor Jankovic and he is someone who actually looked at that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... frame by frame, or as soon as you press your button, does one see the bridge collapse and then it's 6 minutes, 8 seconds count or something like that?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour, on this software it goes second by second. I think there are two options available to us. I know there is some possibility of frame by frame that I saw, I think, on a different video, but also this witness testified yesterday that he's done it frame by frame and I wonder if he has that video with him. May I continue, Mr. President, and I'll ask him that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, but this is the question -- this is the question equals to Dr. Jankovic: Do you have a jumbo jet 747 in your bag? I mean, what are we talking about here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Prosecutor, when one watches the video one can see the bridge collapse but one can't see before that whether there is a flame, smoke, and the water wall or a projectile. That you can't see it in your video here, so you may show it again. But it goes so fast that one can't see. Therefore, let's go forward.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour, it goes second by second, but I'm going to try to open it in a different media player to see if it comes up differently. If I can just have a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Praljak. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honours, I'm not trying to influence the proceedings in any way, but if you look closely, please believe me, you can use any kind of equipment you like to look at this, but there is a cut here, the sort used by film technicians. The part just before the collapse and the destruction itself and right after --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpretation cannot proceed because we have several channels at the same time. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, your assumption, of course I thought about it, but to check it I wanted us to be shown second by second or tenth by tenth of second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I add something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call your attention that passage from one frame to another there should be 4/100ths [Realtime transcript read in error "1/400th"] of a second or 40 milliseconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, is this going to get confusing. The transcript says 1/400th of a second which is not what I understood the witness to say. That just in case that shouldn't get corrected, he said 4/100ths of a second, in other words, 1/25th, which corresponds with 25 frames per second. That's what I understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] It's not possible to play it on a slower version in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Witness, between the last picture or frame that we've seen at 6 minutes, 6 seconds, and 7/10ths, I think, and after that the bridge collapses. According to you, would there be a cut in the picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to know exactly when I have this impression I will look frame by frame, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: You'll remember on this video your water pillar was at 4.26, and although we couldn't see the frame preceding the collapse at 6.08, you will agree with me that that's about a minute and three-quarters later; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if that's -- you've calculated correctly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Well, whether I've calculated correctly or not, it's a considerable amount of more time than you had on your video, right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: You'll agree with me that the TV ORF video that you viewed was either edited, spliced, or was clearly not in the original format?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I accept that.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And you'll agree with me that at least this video suggests to you that there was a greater amount of time between the water pillar and the actual collapse of the bridge?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is to say, this video we've seen, there has been a moment after the water wall and the bridge doesn't collapse for a moment. So according to that film, the bridge was not destroyed by that explosion or by this activation of a detonating cord or the initiating as we have seen and so on. That is obvious, but the collapsing of the bridge in this film, I -- gives me the impression that there is also before the bridge collapses a cut, there is a discontinuity.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, I'm just going to back up and repeat to you. At line 20 you said: "According to that film," which is the film we just watched, "the bridge was not destroyed by that explosion or by this activation of the detonation cord ..." So are you now testifying that, in fact, the water pillar that you saw in this video which you testified to be the same water pillar you saw on TV ORF is not the cause of the collapse of the bridge?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My impression is that there have been two different things. First, the Mostar film shows a continuum, activation and destruction of the bridge. I accept that this film is of bad quality. The film of ORF, which is of much better quality, there is a cut, a splicing. You have more or less the same film also with a cut, but there is a time interval which shows that the water wall and this activation is not the cause of the destruction of the bridge because if it had been the cause, the bridge should have collapsed immediately after.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you, Professor. If that is the case and if that is now what you base your facts on which are quite different than the facts that you based your original report on, then will you agree with me that the TV ORF water pillar we see is not the cause of the collapse of the bridge?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. It is not clearly implied -- or rather, the question implies that the expert is changing his position. The question is not specific enough. It should specify that this is in relation to what we're watching now, which is P 01040, because afterwards if we were to read the transcript, it would just be completely unclear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hold on a second. Mr. Witness, expert, I shall summarize the problem. We have three videos, the Mostar video, the ORF video, on those two videos you have based your own expert report; there's a third video which is being shown at the moment, which is the video which the Prosecutor has introduced. If I make any mistakes, stop me immediately, tell me. In the video presented by the Prosecution it is practically certain, it appears practically certain, that there has been an explosion which does not have -- that doesn't make the bridge collapse. The bridge in this video is going to collapse later, much later.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Later. From that point, if one tries to reconcile the three videos, would the following outline be possible? First, the first attempt which tries to make the bridge collapse, and you can see on video P 1040, one can see smoke, a water wall, but the bridge remains as is. And sometime later we see the smoke, the water wall, and the bridge which collapses. Does this scenario, is it compatible with what you know as an expert? Does it reconcile with the video of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's how I see matters, yes. Therefore, there's a first attempt which it failed, a second attempt which succeeded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Madam Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We're going to move on to the TV Mostar video. Do you recognise this first frame?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And yesterday you saw IC 574, which was a Defence exhibit that was admitted in 2007. You also saw -- then you saw a clearer version of this. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to show it to you again, this is IC 574, it's the same video but just clearer, and I'm just asking if this looks -- excuse me, let me ask you if this looks familiar to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it seems to be -- it looks very much like the Mostar film.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to use this instead for questions because it's a better video if you will agree that it's the same one and we're going to start at the beginning. I'm just going to play it for one second.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now we're at 0.5 and on the right-hand side you see some water activity. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the water gush.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And you also see some water activity in the middle of the river; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see there's -- something has fallen in the water, pieces of rock have fallen in the water.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, if I understand your testimony so far, you will now agree with me that this water activity we see in the right on this video is not the same water pillar that you saw on the TV ORF video?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that isn't the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to continue it a little bit further and I'll remind you about your testimony and the questions yesterday regarding the piece of something that fell off the bridge that we saw right from the middle, if you just keep watching I'll ask you a question.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I'll just stop the video again at 2.9 and I'm going to back it up so you can see it again and ask you whether you see anything falling from the bridge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see the whole bridge collapsing.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Let me ask you another question, Professor. Do you remember from the TV ORF video we actually saw a separate piece fall from the bridge and then it splashed in the water?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So I'm going to ask you whether you see that in this video.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, this water wall which can be seen which might correspond to the Bickford cord which explodes. If this cord explodes, may some pieces of this cord fall further away and make this sort of appearance just by sight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
